data.title: Real-Time Payment Followed by Immediate Refund or Return Request
data.description: Detects a pattern where a real-time payment (RTP or FedNow) is sent and then an immediate refund, return, or Request for Return of Funds (RROF) is submitted within a short window. This pattern may indicate a double-dip fraud scheme where the sender initiates an irrevocable payment, then exploits the refund process to recover funds while the recipient also retains them.

queries.splunk:
`comment("Splunk SPL for Real-Time Payment Followed by Immediate Refund or Return Request")`
`comment("Aggregation that cannot be expressed in Sigma")`
`comment("Original condition: (selection_payment and selection_refund) | temporal(ordered=true, maxspan=2h, by=payment_reference_id)")`
index=flame_banking sourcetype=flame:instant_payments
event_type="instant_payment_completed"
(payment_rail="RTP" OR payment_rail="FEDNOW")
(event_type="refund_request" OR event_type="return_request" OR event_type="rrof_submitted")
| transaction payment_reference_id maxspan=2h
| where eventcount >= 2

falsepositives: Legitimate duplicate payment correction where customer realizes the error immediately
Merchant-initiated refund for cancelled service following immediate payment
